title: A New Approach to Linear Filtering and Prediction Problems (Kalman, 1960) — scalar case
section: Optimal estimate update (scalar form of the filter equations)
excerpt: For a scalar state with prior estimate x̂⁻ and prior variance P⁻, and a measurement z with noise variance R, the optimal (minimum-variance) linear update is: K = P⁻ / (P⁻ + R); x̂ = x̂⁻ + K (z − x̂⁻); P = (1 − K) P⁻. The gain K weighs the measurement residual according to the relative uncertainty of the prediction and the measurement.
focus: Explain the scalar Kalman measurement update as combining two Gaussian beliefs. Let the learner change the prior mean and variance, the measurement and its noise variance. Show the prior, the measurement likelihood and the posterior as bell curves, the gain K, and the updated mean and variance. Check that K is between 0 and 1, that R → 0 trusts the measurement completely (x̂ = z), that P⁻ → 0 ignores it, and that the posterior variance is never larger than either input variance. Explain the assumption of Gaussian noise.
audience: Engineering undergraduate who knows mean, variance and the normal distribution.
